finding.claim: Subscriber-supplied callbackUrl is stored unvalidated and POSTed to by notifyAll every minute, enabling blind SSRF to internal or metadata addresses (MEDIUM: response discarded, ingress and auth unverified).
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe(name, callbackUrl) at src/Jobs.java:13, documented as the body field of POST /subscribe (comment at src/Jobs.java:12)
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) at src/Jobs.java:24, with URI from URI.create(cb) at src/Jobs.java:21

trace.note: subscribe() accepts callbackUrl as a parameter
subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl) stores it with no validation
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI, no scheme, host, or IP check
client.send POSTs payload to the stored URL; response body discarded (blind)

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, hostname allowlist, or IP/CIDR block between store and send. URI.create only parses. Redirects not followed: HttpClient.newHttpClient() at src/Jobs.java:10 defaults to Redirect.NEVER. Response discarded, so blind SSRF capped at MEDIUM. No authentication visible in this file; POST /subscribe route is not in the repo, so ingress and auth unconfirmed.

verdict.guard_found: none. Between the store at src/Jobs.java:14 and the send at src/Jobs.java:24 there is no scheme, host, or IP check. URI.create at line 21 only parses. HttpClient.newHttpClient() at line 10 does not follow redirects by default.
verdict.reason: All five trace lines (13, 14, 19, 21, 24) match the candidate's description and no closing guard exists, but the only evidence that subscribe() is reachable by remote callers is the comment at src/Jobs.java:12, and the POST /subscribe handler, its auth, and any caller are not in the repo (grep finds no other reference to subscribe), so attacker control of callbackUrl cannot be confirmed from the code available.
